newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Peace talks held in Central African Republic.
newsitem.headline: Peace talks held in Central African Republic.

text.p: Army dissidents and African peacekeepers held talks in the Central African Republic capital Bangui on Thursday on how to set the peace process back on track after bloody clashes.
A formal ceasefire, which replaced a four-day truce on Wednesday, held firm.

Witnesses said that Malian mediator Amadou Toumani Toure and the two sides discussed how the army dissidents would return to barracks and hand in weapons to the ambassador of France, the former colonial power. The ambassador was also present.
The meeting also discussed formation of joint patrols with peacekeepers, dissident soldiers and rival soldiers loyal to President Ange-Felix Patasse.

Toumani Toure, Mali's respected former military leader, brokered a deal in January to end three army mutinies in under a year. The mutinies began over pay and conditions but turned into an bid to topple Patasse, a northern civilian elected in 1993.
The clashes between peacekeepers and army dissidents, among a minority who had not rejoined their units under the January deal, followed a June 20 incident between the two sides.
The Red Cross says at least 100 people died in the clashes. Up to 60,000 people fled their homes for the relative safety of the surrounding countryside.
